title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from context (the page itself does not state it). G is a p-divisible group over the ring of integers of a p-adic field, with formal complex multiplication by A, the ring of integers of a finite extension K/Q_p. The case meant is presumably a Lubin–Tate type group: height [K:Q_p], dimension 1. The Tate module T_p = T_p(G) is free of rank 1 over A. π is the Galois group of the base field. It acts on T_p through a character χ_π : π → A^×, the Lubin–Tate character. C is the completed algebraic closure.

(1) Decomposition (*). T_p ⊗_{Z_p} C ≅ A ⊗_{Z_p} C ≅ ∏_σ C_σ. Each C_σ is a copy of C on which A acts through σ : A → C. Since K is assumed Galois and contained in C, there are identifications Hom_{Q_p}(K,C) ≅ Aut_{Q_p}(K) ≅ Aut_{Z_p}(A) ≅ Hom_{Z_p-alg}(A,C).

(2) Galois action. The decomposition is π-stable. On the factor C_σ, g ∈ π acts by x ↦ σ(χ_π(g))·x, understood semilinearly with respect to the Galois action on C.

(3) Comparison with Tate's Hodge–Tate theorem. There is an exact sequence 0 → 𝒱 ⊗ C(1) → T_p ⊗ C → 𝒱̌* ⊗ C → 0, and it splits: T_p ⊗ C ≅ 𝒱 ⊗_A C(1) ⊕ 𝒱̌* ⊗_A C. Here 𝒱 is the tangent space (Lie algebra) of G and 𝒱̌* is the dual of the tangent space of the dual group G'.

(4) Matching by A-action. A acts on the 1-dimensional Lie algebra 𝒱 through the canonical embedding (σ = 1). It acts on 𝒱̌* ⊗ C through the embeddings σ ≠ 1. Since the splitting is A-equivariant, (**) must coincide with the regrouping T_p ⊗ C ≅ C_1 ⊕ ∏_{σ≠1} C_σ. The last line ('En tant qu'isomorphismes can., etc.') starts to say that this also holds as an identification of canonical isomorphisms.

Consequences. C_1 ≅ C(1), i.e. χ_π twisted by the identity embedding has Hodge–Tate weight 1. For σ ≠ 1 the factor C_σ is C-admissible, i.e. Hodge–Tate weight 0. This is the standard computation of the Hodge–Tate weights of the Lubin–Tate character: χ_LT ⊗_{K,σ} C ≅ C(1) if σ = id and ≅ C otherwise.

Purpose. The calculation is a test of Tate's decomposition on the CM / Lubin–Tate example, in the context of Grothendieck's 1970 work on crystals and Dieudonné theory (Barsotti–Tate groups, the 'mysterious functor').
errors: The isomorphism Hom_{Q_p}(K,C) ≅ Aut_{Q_p}(K) needs K/Q_p Galois and a chosen embedding K ⊂ C. This is implicit in the notes.
The action of π on C_σ is semilinear: g acts as x ↦ σ(χ(g))·g(x), not as plain multiplication. The formula on the page is shorthand.
The first exact sequence is missing its initial 0; '+' in (**) means direct sum; ∏ over σ is a finite product, i.e. a direct sum.

The matching of (**) with (*) is asserted but not fully justified. One needs Tate's splitting to be A-equivariant and the σ-isotypic parts to be distinct; this is fine since the embeddings σ are pairwise distinct.

ideas.what: Decomposition of T_p ⊗ C for a CM p-divisible group into eigenlines C_σ indexed by embeddings of K, with Galois acting by σ∘χ
ideas.modern_name: Isotypic decomposition of A ⊗_{Z_p} C; Galois action via the Lubin–Tate character

ideas.what: Comparison with Tate's Hodge–Tate decomposition T_p ⊗ C ≅ (Lie G ⊗ C(1)) ⊕ (t_{G'}^* ⊗ C), showing C_1 ≅ C(1) and C_σ ≅ C for σ ≠ 1
ideas.modern_name: Hodge–Tate weights of the Lubin–Tate character (weight 1 at the identity embedding, 0 elsewhere)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification of Tate's Hodge–Tate decomposition on the Lubin–Tate/CM example, a computation already in Tate (1967) and Serre (1968). Its only interest is documentary: it shows Grothendieck testing Tate's theorem while working on crystals in 1970.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads: 'où C_σ = C comme C-module, l'opération de A donnée en faisant via σ : A → C, où'.
The first exact sequence should begin with '0 →': 0 → 𝒱 ⊗ C(1) → T_p ⊗ C → 𝒱̌* ⊗ C → 0.
'Notons que le dernier terme est facteur [?]' plausibly reads '... facteur direct'.
Lower half: 'Notons que A opère sur les deux membres'. 'l'action régulière' may instead be 'l'action naturelle/évidente', i.e. via σ = 1; the image is ambiguous.
Near the end: 'Donc la décomposition (**) de T_p ⊗ C est celle déduite de la décomposition (*) en l'écrivant T_p ⊗ C ≅ C_1 ⊕ ∏_{σ≠1} C_σ'.
The neighbouring-page transcriptions (Bourbaki-style typescript nos. 4.12–4.13 on manifolds) belong to the faint typed sheet showing through on the reverse, not to the mathematics of these notes.
